title: Crossregion traffic sandbox and standby validation lab
creator: Aisha Nambiar
description:
Objective:
Build a reproducible cross-region "traffic sandbox" and a warm-standby validation lab that can be used by the routing controller to certify readiness of standby fleets and fallback model variants before doing real cutovers. The sandbox will exercise region selection, tier routing, and model-variant fallbacks under realistic latency/capacity distributions and produce a readiness score used by the failover orchestrator.

Background and motivation:
We currently rely on ad-hoc warmup probes and synthetic liveness pings to determine standby fitness for regional failovers. Those probes don’t exercise the full routing stack (tier rules, prefix/KV cache hit ratios, model variant negotiations) and have surfaced gaps during live cutovers (cold KV caches, mismatched quantization profiles, and model variant output regressions). This ticket creates an isolated environment that simulates cross-region traffic and validates readiness end-to-end without impacting production.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: sandbox harness, traffic generator (latency/calls-per-second shapes), readiness scoring service, integration hooks for routing controller, automated pre-cutover certification job, dashboards, and alert thresholds.
- Out of scope: procurement of additional GPUs (we will reuse staging Dedicated pools and ephemeral dev capacity) and building new model conversion tooling.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A standalone sandbox environment that can replay a configurable traffic profile (percentiles for RTT, token length, request distribution across endpoints) to a candidate standby region.
2) Readiness score (0-100) computed from: latency SLO compliance, tail latency (p99), throughput priming (tokens/sec baseline), KV cache warm fraction, model-variant output similarity (embedding cos sim / token-level perplexity delta), and error-rate.
3) End-to-end automated certification run that updates the routing controller with a signed readiness assertion when score >= 85.
4) Dashboards and traces for each run (latency breakdown per kernel, batch sizes observed, cache hit trajectory) and a synthetic traffic trace stored in the observability bucket.
5) Runbook with go/no-go checks, rollback triggers, and a staged cutover checklist.

Design plan (high level):
1) Traffic sandbox orchestrator: Kubernetes job that can deploy an isolated traffic generator and target agent in a staging VPC. The generator can produce distributions (uniform, bimodal, heavy-tailed) and parameterize token lengths, streaming vs non-streaming, and tool-calls.
2) Readiness probe agent: lightweight agent deployed to standby fleet nodes to collect KV cache metrics, batch behavior, kernel selection counts, and model variant negotiation logs (which variant served, quantization used). Agent uploads artifacts to the sandbox results store.
3) Scoring service: serverless function that pulls artifacts, computes feature signals (cache warm fraction, p95 delta from baseline, model similarity), and emits a single readiness score plus component breakdown.
4) Controller integration: routing controller accepts a signed certificate with expiry and score vector. Certification job will be scheduled on every fleet refresh and before manual cross-region reroutes.

Test matrix and scenarios:
- Cold start stress: priming from 0% cache to target traffic within 5 minutes, measure cost of prefill and time-to-SLO.
- Partial variant fallback: route 20% traffic to a compressed variant and evaluate output drift and latency improvements.
- Degraded capacity: simulate 70% CPU/GPU load and observe routing decisioning under tiered fallback.
- Cross-region RTT shift: increase RTT to standby and ensure controller falls back to alternative tier when score drops below threshold.

Observability and metrics to add:
- readiness.score (gauge), readiness.component.* (gauges), sandbox.run_id (tag), probe.cache_warm_fraction, probe.batch_size_histogram, model.similarity_cosine_p99, model.perplexity_delta_p95.
- Trace hooks: annotate trace spans with kernel selection and quantization path to debug regressions.

Runbook highlights:
- If readiness.score < 50 during certification: abort cutover and mark fleet as quarantined; schedule a warm-prefill and re-run.
- If model.similarity_cosine_p99 < 0.92: block automated promotion and create a model-eval task under project "Model Onboarding QA".

Dependencies and risks:
- Depends on staging access to Dedicated pools (ENG-198210).
- Requires small enhancements to the routing controller API (accept signed readiness certificates) — tracked in ENG-214582.
- Risk: synthetic traffic might not cover rare tail patterns found in production; mitigate by seeding sandbox profiles with sampled production traces (privacy-reviewed).

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1: traffic generator + probe agent prototype (P0 metric outputs).
- Week 2: scoring service + basic dashboard; integrate with controller for READINESS dry-run.
- Week 3: chaos scenarios and runbook, automated certification job, and initial production pilot with one customer region.

Longer-term ideas (out of scope for this ticket but captured):
- Automated warm-prefill controller that opportunistically replays hot prefixes into standby KV caches based on production token streams.
- Continuous certification: scheduled daily sandbox runs with trending and anomaly alerts.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Traffic+Sandbox+Design
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sandbox-sim
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/standby/sandbox-readiness
- Routing controller PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/482

Acceptance test runbook (short):
1) Trigger sandbox with profile "eu-high-rt-heavy-tokens".
2) Wait for run_id to appear in the dashboard and confirm probe.cache_warm_fraction >= 0.6 within 10m.
3) Verify readiness.score >= 85 and certificate issued.
4) Perform a controlled 5% traffic canary to standby for 10m and verify p99 latency within SLO.
